arguments.sql_query:
WITH cv_categories AS (
    SELECT 'Hypertension' AS category, 316866 AS ancestor_concept_id
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Coronary/ischemic heart disease', 4185932
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Heart failure', 316139
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Atrial fibrillation', 313217
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Cerebrovascular disease', 381591
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Peripheral vascular disease', 321052
), person_cv AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id, c.category
    FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
    JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca
      ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
    JOIN cv_categories c
      ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = c.ancestor_concept_id
), person_counts AS (
    SELECT person_id, COUNT(*) AS cv_category_count
    FROM person_cv
    GROUP BY person_id
), denom AS (
    SELECT p.gender_concept_id, gc.concept_name AS sex, COUNT(*) AS denominator
    FROM omop.person p
    LEFT JOIN omop.concept gc ON p.gender_concept_id = gc.concept_id
    WHERE p.gender_concept_id IN (8507, 8532)
    GROUP BY p.gender_concept_id, gc.concept_name
)
SELECT d.sex,
       d.denominator,
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.cv_category_count,0) >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cardiovascular_multimorbidity_n,
       CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.cv_category_count,0) >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / d.denominator AS DECIMAL(6,2)) AS cardiovascular_multimorbidity_percent,
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.cv_category_count,0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cv_categories_0,
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.cv_category_count,0) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cv_categories_1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(pc.cv_category_count,0) >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cv_categories_2plus
FROM denom d
JOIN omop.person p ON p.gender_concept_id = d.gender_concept_id
LEFT JOIN person_counts pc ON p.person_id = pc.person_id
GROUP BY d.sex, d.denominator
ORDER BY d.sex;

Using OMOP `person` as the cohort denominator and defining cardiovascular multimorbidity as **≥2 distinct cardiovascular condition categories** among hypertension, coronary/ischemic heart disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, cerebrovascular disease, and peripheral vascular disease:

| Sex | Cohort N | CV multimorbidity N | Frequency |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Female | 3,807,338 | 82,787 | 2.17% |
| Male | 3,269,779 | 102,320 | 3.13% |

So, cardiovascular multimorbidity was more frequent in men than women in this cohort: **3.13% vs 2.17%**.

Caveat: this uses a broad diagnosis-code phenotype over all recorded OMOP condition history, not an age-adjusted or time-windowed estimate.
